Key Research Thinking Patterns: Distributional Debiasing via Kernel Alignment: Correcting self-labeling biases in social network analysis by integrating text embeddings with Kernel Means Matching to align training and testing distributions, thereby reducing generalization error in demographic prediction tasks.

Decoupled Fairness-Aware Active Learning: Selecting data instances based on prediction disagreements between group-specific models to minimize alpha-distance, effectively balancing accuracy and disparate impact fairness in active learning scenarios without sacrificing predictive performance.

Data-Dependent Random Projection for Computational Efficiency: Accelerating large-scale least squares regression by mapping data into the row space of a randomly projected matrix, achieving exponentially decaying empirical excess risk while maintaining data reconstruction fidelity more efficiently than data-independent methods.

Prototype-Based Modality and Class Balancing: Addressing multimodal and class imbalances in fake news detection by employing modality and class prototypes with constrained gradient optimization to balance feature distributions and enhance class separability, significantly improving detection accuracy on imbalanced datasets.
Summary Description: Chao Lan specializes in computational social systems, focusing on algorithmic fairness, efficient machine learning, and multimodal analysis. The researcher develops novel theoretical frameworks and algorithms to address bias in demographic prediction and misinformation detection on social platforms. Key contributions include debiased text learning using Kernel Means Matching, fairness-aware active learning via decoupled model disagreement, and high-dimensional data acceleration through data-dependent random projections. Additionally, Lan advances multimodal fake news detection by implementing prototype-based balancing strategies to handle modality and class imbalances. The work bridges statistical learning theory with practical applications in social media analysis, AI recruitment, and public opinion monitoring, emphasizing both computational efficiency and ethical AI deployment.
